title: Fixed point
summary: A fixed point is a state left unchanged by a map.

context.note: Revision 2 exposes a QEVA foundation dependency instead of stopping only at a textual framework label.

assumptions.text: A set X and a map F:X→X are specified.

content.plain: A fixed point reproduces itself after one application of the update rule.
content.exact: x*∈X is a fixed point of F iff F(x*)=x*.
content.example: For F(x)=x^2 on R, 0 and 1 are fixed points.
content.caveat: A fixed point may be stable, unstable, attracting, repelling, or neutral depending on additional structure and the chosen stability notion.

relations.note: Stability asks how nearby states behave.
A fixed point is a period-1 point.
